overall_reason: The scene is a cool slate system: a #1f2936 stage, a lighter #303a45 window, a #405263 selected row and a white preview card, with text greys #dce3e9, #9caab7 and #87929d all on one cool temperature.

score.reason: T-NEUTRALS and T-DARK-MODE pass (one cool temperature, raised surfaces lighter than the stage), but T-SURFACE-LADDER finds two heavy black shadows on a dark stage where lightness already separates the layers.

findings.title: Depth comes from lightness and one shadow
findings.evidence: The palette table finds 2 shadow recipes, both counted as heavy black shadows: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.533) 0 20px 40px -18px' and 'rgba(0,0,0,0.4) 0 16px 32px -12px'.
findings.before: Two black shadows at 0.4 and 0.53 alpha
findings.after: One shadow recipe, lighter and tinted toward the slate hue; let the lightness steps carry the layering
findings.why: On a dark stage a black shadow is almost invisible, so the second recipe adds weight without adding depth.

strengths: Raised surfaces get lighter on dark: stage #1f2936, window #303a45, selected row #405263 (CLR-017 kept).
All neutrals hold one cool temperature (20 of 21 text and fill neutrals in hue 180 to 300).
not_investigated: Brand authority: the run has no 00-contract.md, so no brand colours or design system were available; T-COLOUR-SOURCE was judged from the composition alone, and the visitor mode was taken as Operate (a product UI component).
T-GRADIENT-STOPS and contrast: owned by the sweep (A11-001); small-text contrast hits are not restated here.
T-DARK-MODE: run on the dark product window shown in the scene; the page's own dark class theme was not rendered and is not verified.
